title: Reading the YAML DSL
summary: Read a route file top to bottom, and the Simple expression language it is full of.

steps.title: A route file
body: Camel routes can be written in Java, XML or **YAML**. Visual designers such as Karavan and Kaoto read and write
the YAML DSL. A file is a **list**; each top-level `-` item is a route (or a configuration).
Read it as: *on* `GET /books/{isbn}`, log, set a header, set the body. When the last step finishes, the body
and the headers become the HTTP response.

steps.prompt: What does `GET /books/9780131103627` return with the route above?
options: `204 No Content`, because nothing called a backend
`404`, because no backend knows the book
steps.explain: The path parameter became the header `isbn`. `log` only writes to the log; `setBody` decides the response. A route needs no backend to answer.

steps.title: Simple, Constant and placeholders
body: Most step options take an **expression**. The languages you will meet most:
- **Constant**: a fixed text, no evaluation. Cheapest and safest when nothing varies.
- **Property placeholders** `{{catalogue.url}}` and `{{env:CATALOGUE_URL}}`: filled **once at startup** from
> **Tip:** some project templates (Karavan's among them) set `camel.main.logLanguage = groovy`, so `log` messages
> are Groovy (`"looking up " + headers.isbn`), not Simple. A message copied from the docs must then be translated.

steps.prompt: Match each expression to what it gives.
pairs: A value stored with `setVariable`, never sent anywhere
The exchange's unique id, a ready-made trace id
A configuration value filled in at startup

steps.prompt: Complete the router: GB orders go to `direct:domestic`, all others to `direct:international`.
steps.explain: `choice` / `when` / `otherwise` is Camel's `if / else`. Simple compares with `==`; a single `=` is not an operator.
A missing header evaluates to nothing, silently. That is why a typo in a header name gives you a URL with an empty segment rather than an error.

steps.prompt: A route logs `looking up ${header.isbn}` but the log shows exactly that text, braces and all. The project sets `camel.main.logLanguage = groovy`. What is going on?
options: Log messages are evaluated as Groovy in this project, so the Simple syntax is not interpreted; write it as Groovy or remove the setting
steps.explain: Know which language each option is evaluated in. The log language setting changes only `log` steps; `toD` URIs and `simple:` options are still Simple.

steps.title: A tiny Simple language
prompt: Write `string Simple(string expr, Exchange ex)` that replaces every `${...}` in `expr`:
- `${variable.NAME}` → that variable's `ToString()`, or `""` if missing (or null);
- anything else inside `${...}` → throw `ArgumentException` (a typo should fail loudly in *your* language).
Text outside `${...}` is kept as is. A `Regex.Replace` with a `MatchEvaluator` is the natural tool.
solution: if (key.StartsWith("header.")) return ex.Headers.TryGetValue(key["header.".Length..], out var h) ? h : "";
if (key.StartsWith("variable.")) return ex.Variables.TryGetValue(key["variable.".Length..], out var v) ? v?.ToString() ?? "" : "";
hints: `Regex.Replace(expr, @"\$\{([^}]+)\}", m => ...)` gives you each key in `m.Groups[1].Value`.
Check `StartsWith("header.")` and slice off the prefix to get the name.
template: var dojoEx = new Exchange { Id = "ex-42", Body = "{\"a\":1}" };
Dojo.Eq("header names are case-insensitive", "9780131103627", Simple("${header.ISBN}", dojoEx));
Dojo.Eq("text without expressions is unchanged", "plain text", Simple("plain text", dojoEx));
Dojo.Throws<ArgumentException>("unknown expression fails loudly", () => Simple("${heder.isbn}", dojoEx));
public Dictionary<string, string> Headers { get; } = new(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
public Dictionary<string, object?> Variables { get; } = new();
